> **AI agents: read https://finchmcp.com/agents.md first.** It is the step-by-step guide for publishing a local MCP server with finch on your human's behalf: install, a two-step login with one human approval, `finch add`, `finch service install`, `finch test`, and `finch connect`, plus the exit codes, the JSON error format, and the security rules. Follow it rather than the summary below.

# finch

> finch turns a local MCP server (or any local HTTP app) on your own machine into a stable public https endpoint. The machine dials out to finch, so nothing listens and no ports open. Auth is checked at the edge before a request reaches your machine. Clients reach an MCP server at https://<slug>.finchmcp.com/<name>/mcp, where <slug> is the account address finch assigns at sign-up, with an Authorization: Bearer finch_<key> header or by signing in with OAuth. A service can also be made public (no key needed).

finch is operated from a CLI on macOS and Linux. Every command accepts --json: success payloads carry "schema_version":1 and use snake_case field names, and errors go to stderr as {"schema_version":1,"error":{"code","message","next"}}. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 10 waiting for approval, 11 expired, 12 not logged in. The installed binary prints the agent manual (the same text as agents.md) with `finch guide`, and `finch help <command>` shows one command's flags and an example.

By default finch forwards only /<name>/mcp. For a web app or a REST API, publish it with `finch add <name> --service <url> --forward-all`, and finch forwards every path under /<name>/.

Agent flow: `finch status --json` (no "schema_version":1 in its output, or a "version" below 1.7.0, means an older finch: install 1.7.0 or later first) → `finch login --start --json` (show the human the link and code) → `finch login --poll --json` every `interval` seconds until exit 0 → `finch add <name> --service http://127.0.0.1:<port> --json` (prints the public URL) → `finch service install --json` (runs `finch run` as a launchd or systemd user service) → `finch test <name> --json` → `finch connect <name> --client claude-code|cursor|codex|json`. `finch connect` mints a finch_ key for that client and writes it into the client's config without printing it.

The one paste for humans: "Read https://finchmcp.com/agents.md and use finch to publish my MCP server on http://127.0.0.1:8000 as notes. Show me the sign-in link when you get it. Run it as a background service, check it with finch test, then connect it to this agent."

## Base case: hello world, end to end

```bash
pip install fastmcp
cat > server.py <<'EOF'
from fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("hello")

@mcp.tool
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    """Say hello."""
    return f"Hello, {name}!"

if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run(transport="http", port=8000)
EOF
python server.py &                                   # serves MCP on http://127.0.0.1:8000

curl -fsSL https://finchmcp.com/install | sh         # install finch (macOS/Linux, never prompts for sudo)
finch login                                          # opens your browser; approve on any device (phone ok)
finch add hello --service http://127.0.0.1:8000      # writes ~/.finch/finch.yml (no secrets), prints the public URL
finch service install                                # keeps it running (launchd / systemd --user)

finch test hello                                     # lists the greet tool; non-zero exit if it fails
finch call hello greet --args '{"name": "world"}'    # -> Hello, world!
finch connect hello --client claude-code             # wires it into Claude Code with a fresh finch_ key
finch logs hello                                     # the recent calls: time, route, caller, status, duration
```

An agent logs in with the two-step form instead (`finch login --start --json`, then `finch login --poll --json` until exit 0), as agents.md describes.

Later: `finch add hello --service http://127.0.0.1:9000` again changes the local URL in place; `finch fleet` lists every service with its public URL; `finch rm hello` removes it from the account and this machine; `finch uninstall` removes finch's background service, logins, the keys and client entries `finch connect` made, and ~/.finch (it prints how to delete the binary).

## Docs

- [Agent guide](https://finchmcp.com/agents.md): the step-by-step agent flow, exit codes, error table, and security rules
- [Quickstart](https://finchmcp.com/docs): install, log in, add a service, run, connect a client
- [AviaryMCP](https://finchmcp.com/docs/aviarymcp): public Python SDK release candidate on PyPI; one tool registry for MCP, REST, and OpenAPI, published with `finch add` like any local service
- [Services & boxes](https://finchmcp.com/docs/services): the service/box model, finch.yml, running as a background service, states
- [Keys & auth](https://finchmcp.com/docs/auth): finch_ keys, mint/list/revoke, the CLI admin token, how auth is checked at the edge
- [Access control](https://finchmcp.com/docs/acls): finch_ keys scoped per service, OAuth, public services; one key per agent
- [Domains](https://finchmcp.com/docs/domains): the automatic <slug>.finchmcp.com hub domain and custom hostnames
- [CLI reference](https://finchmcp.com/docs/cli): every command, the JSON and exit-code contract, and the finch.yml format

## Install

- [Install script](https://finchmcp.com/install): `curl -fsSL https://finchmcp.com/install | sh` (macOS and Linux). It never prompts for sudo: it installs to /usr/local/bin when you can write it and no other user can, otherwise to ~/.local/bin (and prints a PATH hint). Set FINCH_INSTALL_DIR to choose the directory; one that other users can write (group- or world-writable without the sticky bit) is refused.

## Optional

- [Pricing](https://finchmcp.com/#pricing): free for individuals; Enterprise (SLA, support, security review) by email

## AviaryMCP release candidate

AviaryMCP 0.1.0rc6 is public on PyPI (`python -m pip install 'aviary-mcp==0.1.0rc6'`). Read the [project-specific machine-readable guide](/aviarymcp-llms.txt) on this origin. It subclasses FastMCP and follows the normal FastMCP convention: create `mcp = AviaryMCP("My MCP Server")`, register tools with `@mcp.tool`, and call `mcp.run()`. Serve it on loopback and publish it like any other local service:

```python
from aviary_mcp import AviaryMCP

mcp = AviaryMCP("calculator")

@mcp.tool
def add(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return a + b

mcp.run(transport="http", host="127.0.0.1", port=8000)
```

```bash
finch add calculator --service http://127.0.0.1:8000
finch service install
```

AviaryMCP exposes the same registered tools at `/mcp`, `/api/v1/tools`, `/api/v1/tools/<tool>`, and `/api/v1/openapi.json`. finch forwards only `/calculator/mcp` unless the service is added with `--forward-all` (`finch add calculator --service http://127.0.0.1:8000 --forward-all`); with it, all of them answer under `https://<slug>.finchmcp.com/calculator/`.
